title: American Airlines 625
summary: Maximum flap setting of 40 degrees was never applied; aircraft speed was 10 knots higher than VREF. Aircraft floated from turbulent winds. Aircraft touched down 2300 feet down the 4658 foot runway. Pilot attempted go-around with only 700 feet left but engines slow responding. Pilot panicked and applied full brakes. The aircraft overran and crashed into Shell gas station killing 37 people.
probable_cause: The captain's failure to apply maximum flap setting and failure to execute timely go-around; pilot panicked and reversed thrust applied too late.

factors.evidence: maximum flap setting of 40 degrees was never applied, which meant that the aircraft's speed was 10 kn higher than VREF
aircraft floated from turbulent winds in the area
captain did not have awareness that when he touched down 2300 ft down the 4658 ft runway, he did not have enough distance to perform a go-around
pilot proceeded to apply full throttle three seconds after touchdown in an attempt at a go-around; after five seconds of waiting for power, pilot panicked and applied full brakes
pilot forgot to apply reverse engine thrust until immediately before impact
aircraft ran off the end of the runway and into a Shell gas station

events.text: Aircraft in approach at high speed with maximum flap setting of 40 degrees never applied
Aircraft floated from turbulent winds in the area
When he touched down 2300 ft down the 4658 ft runway, he did not have enough distance
Pilot proceeded to apply full throttle three seconds after touchdown in an attempt at a go-around
After five seconds of waiting for power, pilot panicked and applied full brakes; pilot forgot to apply reverse engine thrust until immediately before impact
Aircraft ran off the end of the runway and into a Shell gas station
